summary: Gyurme Pema Tekchok studied under Dilgo Khyentse and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.
György Hazai was a linguist and Central Asian specialist who studied at Eötvös Loránd University (~1950–1954). He held a post at the Institut für Orientforschung from circa 1963 to 1982.

György Kara worked in linguistics and Central Asian studies. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University under Gyula Németh and Lajos Ligeti, and held posts at ELTE, the Hungarian Academy of Sciences (1975–2000), and Indiana University (1993–2022).
Gyōin Hashimoto studied Buddhist studies and philosophy at the University of Tokyo (~1921–1925) under Join Saeki. He served as kanshu of Yakushiji (1939–1967) and kanchō of Hōssō-shū (1940).
Gé Mang Khenchen Yönten Gyatso studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and he taught Shechen Gyaltsab.

Gérard Colas is an Indologist. He has held posts as a research director and senior fellow at the CNRS (attested 2004, 2009) and at the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences (attested 2012).

Gérard Fussman studied at the École Normale Supérieure (~1960–1965), working in Indology, history, archaeology, and linguistics. He served as a professor at the Collège de France starting in 1984 and headed a unit at the CNRS (attested 1994).

Géza Bethlenfalvy studied Tibetology and Indology at Eötvös Loránd University (1956–1963) under Lajos Ligeti. He held posts at the University of Delhi (1970), Eötvös Loránd University, and the Hungarian Academy of Sciences, and visited the University of Vienna (2007–2008).

Gösta Liebert was an Indologist and linguist who earned his doctorate from the University of Gothenburg (~1944–1949), studying under Hjalmar Frisk, Nils Holmer, and Stig Wikander. He served as professor at the University of Gothenburg (1955–1982).

Götz von Selle studied at Berlin, Kiel, and Göttingen (Dr. phil. ~1918–1920). A historian and Central Asian specialist, he worked at the Göttingen library and served as professor and deputy library director at the University of Königsberg (~1938–1945).
Günter Blamberger held posts at the University of Kassel (~1990–1993) and served as Chair in German Philology at the University of Cologne (~1993–2017).

Günter Grönbold worked in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the Bavarian State Library from circa 1973 to 2008, heading its South Asia Department (~1976) and Oriental Section (~1988–2008).

Günter Schweiger studied at the Vienna University of Economics and Business (~1959–1963) and under doctoral supervisor Gert Klingenschmitt. A scholar in linguistics and Central Asian studies, he was an ordinary university professor at WU Vienna from 1974 to 2009.

Linguist H. Craig Melchert studied at Michigan State, the Defense Language Institute, the National Cryptologic School, and Harvard (~1971–1977). He held posts at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (1978–2007) and UCLA (2007–2015).

H. D. Sankalia was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at University College London (~1934–1936). He served as an archaeologist at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (1945–1946).

Indologist H. G. Narahari studied at the University of Mysore and the University of Madras, where C. Kunhan Raja supervised his MA. By 1944, he was a research assistant at Adyar Library and a research fellow at the University of Madras.
H. J. de Graaf worked in history and archaeology, studying at Leiden University (~1919–1935) and under Poerbatjaraka between 1927 and 1930.
H. Kikuchi was a research student at the University of Delhi in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying under Vasudev Vishwanath Gokhale (attested 1966).
H. Sesha Aiyangar was an Indologist and linguist who held posts in the Kannaḍa and Canarese departments at the University of Madras (attested 1938 and 1957).
H. V. Nagaraja Rao works in Indology, philosophy, and linguistics. He held posts at the Oriental Research Institute Mysore and served as professor at the University of Mysore (attested 2012).
